description: A RECENT STUDY IN PLASTID GENETIC ENGINEERING FROM THE PDS' LABORATORIES HAS GREATLY ADVANCED CHLOROPLAST METABOLIC ENGINEERING OF VALUABLE HETEROLOGOUS TERPENES, WHICH CREATES PROMISING NEW OPPORTUNITIES TO ENHANCE CROP RESILIENCE TO NATURAL ENEMIES AND ABIOTIC STRESSES. FIRST, THE PDS DEVELOPED A MAJOR INNOVATION IN SOLANUM TUBEROSUM (POTATO) PLASTID ENGINEERING BY COMBINING A NOVEL SITE-SPECIFIC TRANSFORMATION VECTOR WITH ENDOGENOUS PLASTID REGULATORY ELEMENTS, ENABLING STRONG TRANSGENE EXPRESSION WITHOUT COMPROMISING PLANT PHENOTYPE. SECOND, THIS PLATFORM WAS SUCCESSFULLY USED TO EXPRESS VALUABLE TERPENE-PRODUCING GENES IN CHLOROPLASTS, GENERATING TRANSPLASTOMIC POTATO LINES WITH NORMAL GROWTH AND STRONG POTENTIAL AS IMPROVED TRAITS. BEFORE THESE NOVEL LINES CAN BE SAFELY RELEASED, A RIGOROUS ENVIRONMENTAL RISK ASSESSMENT IS ESSENTIAL. THIS PROJECT WILL EVALUATE THE ECOLOGICAL EFFECTS OF THREE TRANSPLASTOMIC POTATO GENOTYPES PRODUCING MONOTERPENES, SESQUITERPENES, AND DITERPENES RESPECTIVELY THAT ARE ALREADY AVAILABLE IN THE PDS' LABORATORIES. FOLLOWING COMPREHENSIVE PHENOTYPIC CHARACTERIZATION AND SELECTION OF THE TOP-PERFORMING LINE, WE WILL ASSESS EFFECTS ON TARGET HERBIVORES, BENEFICIAL NON-TARGET INSECTS, NEIGHBORING CROP AND WEED SPECIES, SOIL MICROBIAL COMMUNITIES, AND SOIL PHYSICOCHEMICAL PROPERTIES. BY DELIVERING THIS COMPREHENSIVE ECOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT, THIS STUDY WILL SUPPORT SAFE AGRICULTURAL USE OF TERPENE-PRODUCING TRANSPLASTOMIC POTATO VARIETIES. THIS PROJECT IS STRONGLY ALIGNED WITH THE USDA BRAG PRIORITY AREA, EFFECTS OF GE ORGANISMS RELATIVE TO NON-GE ORGANISMS IN THE CONTEXT OF PRODUCTION SYSTEMS, PARTICULARLY ITS EMPHASIS ON UNDERSTANDING AND INFORMING REGULATORY AGENCIES ON UNINTENDED ECOLOGICAL EFFECTS OF GE ORGANISMS TO MICROBES, ANIMALS, AND RELATED SPECIES.

description: THIS PROJECT AIMS TO OPTIMIZE AND FURTHER SCALE UP AN IN-LINE FLOW-THROUGH AND CHEMICAL-FREE UV TREATMENT TRAIN TOWARDS COMMERCIALIZINGPFAS DESTRUCTION IN AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD INDUSTRY APPLICATIONS. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES PRESSING GLOBAL CONTAMINATION RISKS OF PER- AND POLY-FLUOROALKYL SUBSTANCES (PFAS) - ALSO KNOWN AS FOREVER CHEMICALS - IN IRRIGATION WATER AND FOOD PROCESSING WATER RESOURCES, E.G., GROUNDWATER AND RECYCLED MUNICIPAL WASTEWATER EFFLUENT THROUGH A NOVEL DESTRUCTION TECHNOLOGY. THE ABILITY TO COMPLETELY DESTROY PFAS IN AMBIENT ENVIRONMENT USING CHEMICAL-FREE UV LIGHT WITHOUT GENERATING SECONDARY WASTE OR TOXIC BYPRODUCTS WILL FACILITATE NEW AND COMMERCIALLY VIABLE TECHNOLOGIES TO MITIGATE PFAS AND ENABLE COST-EFFECTIVE NONTRADITIONAL WATER REUSE FOR CROP PRODUCTION. THE OVERARCHING GOAL IS SUPPORTED BY WELL-DESIGNEDTASKS TO SCALE UPAN IN-LINE FLOW-THROUGH PILOT-SCALE UV SYSTEM AND OPTIMIZE THE UV TREATMENT TRAIN AND ITS AUTOMATIONFOR PFAS DESTRUCTION IN AGRICUTURE AND FOOD INDUSTRY. THE PROJECT DIRECTLY ADDRESSESTHEPROGRAM AREA PRIORITIES ON WATER QUANTITY AND QUALITY, AND CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES. IT WILL IMPROVE AGRICULTURE SUSTAINABILITY AND HEALTH BY DEVELOPING AN INNOVATIVE PFAS TREATMENT FOR NON-TRADITIONAL WATER IRRIGATION AND WATER REUSE.

description: FRESH AND FRESH-CUT PRODUCE ARE VULNERABLE TO MICROBIAL CONTAMINATION DURING POSTHARVEST PROCESSING, LEADING TO FOOD SAFETY RISKS, RECALLS, AND FOOD WASTE. THIS PROJECT WILL ADVANCE A FOOD-GRADE ANTIMICROBIAL DISINFECTANT (FAD), A SHELF-STABLE POWDER BASED ON HYDROGEN PEROXIDE. PHASE I DEMONSTRATED ITS ANTIMICROBIAL EFFECTIVENESS AND FEASIBILITY. PHASE II WILL OPTIMIZE PRODUCTION AND STABILITY, EVALUATE ANTIMICROBIAL EFFICACY AND PRODUCT QUALITY, AND VALIDATE PERFORMANCE IN COMMERCIAL PRODUCE WASH SYSTEMS. THE GOAL IS TO PROVIDE THE FRESH PRODUCE INDUSTRY WITH A SAFE, EFFECTIVE, AND SCALABLE ANTIMICROBIAL WASH TECHNOLOGY.

description: FARMERS DEPEND ON INSECTS IN TWO VERY DIFFERENT WAYS: POLLINATORS SUCH AS BEES AND BUTTERFLIES HELP PRODUCE CROPS, WHILE INSECT PESTS CAN DAMAGE CROPS AND REDUCE THEIR VALUE. YET GROWERS AND THEIR ADVISERS OFTEN HAVE LIMITED INFORMATION ABOUT WHEN THESE INSECTS ARE PRESENT, HOW ABUNDANT THEY ARE, AND HOW THEIR ACTIVITY CHANGES ACROSS A FARM OR THROUGHOUT THE DAY. CURRENT MONITORING OFTEN DEPENDS ON OCCASIONAL FIELD VISITS, TRAPS, OR CAMERAS THAT REQUIRE SUBSTANTIAL POWER AND PRODUCE LARGE AMOUNTS OF DATA THAT MUST BE REVIEWED. THIS CAN MAKE IT DIFFICULT TO DETECT EMERGING PEST PROBLEMS, UNDERSTAND WHETHER POLLINATORS ARE PROVIDING ADEQUATE SERVICE, OR MAKE WELL-TIMED DECISIONS ABOUT PESTICIDE USE, BENEFICIAL INSECTS, HABITAT MANAGEMENT, AND COMMERCIAL BEE HIVES. BETTER INFORMATION COULD HELP FARMERS PROTECT CROPS AND INCOME WHILE REDUCING UNNECESSARY CHEMICAL APPLICATIONS AND SUPPORTING NATIVE POLLINATORS AND OTHER BENEFICIAL INSECTS.THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP AND FIELD-TEST A SMALL, BATTERY-POWERED SMART CAMERA SYSTEM THAT CAN CONTINUOUSLY MONITOR INSECTS IN AGRICULTURAL SETTINGS. THE SYSTEM WILL COMBINE CAMERAS, ENVIRONMENTAL SENSORS, AND LOW-POWER MOTION-SENSING TECHNOLOGY TO DETECT INSECT ACTIVITY, DISTINGUISH DIFFERENT TYPES OF INSECT MOVEMENTS AND BEHAVIORS, AND SEND USEFUL SUMMARIES FROM REMOTE PARTS OF FARMS. DEVICES WILL BE TESTED DURING REPEATED FIELD DEPLOYMENTS UNDER DIFFERENT CROP, WEATHER, LIGHTING, AND INSECT CONDITIONS, AND THEIR RESULTS WILL BE CHECKED AGAINST VIDEO OBSERVATIONS AND OTHER FIELD DATA. FARMERS, PEST CONTROL ADVISERS, RESEARCHERS, AND AGRICULTURAL EXTENSION PERSONNEL WILL ALSO PROVIDE FEEDBACK ON THE USEFULNESS OF THE INFORMATION AND HOW IT SHOULD BE PRESENTED. THE ULTIMATE GOAL IS TO PROVIDE GROWERS WITH PRACTICAL, TIMELY INFORMATION ABOUT PESTS AND POLLINATORS SO THEY CAN MAKE BETTER-INFORMED MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. IF SUCCESSFUL, THE TECHNOLOGY COULD HELP REDUCE CROP LOSSES AND UNNECESSARY PESTICIDE USE, IMPROVE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF POLLINATION AND HABITAT-MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, LOWER MONITORING COSTS, AND PROVIDE RESEARCHERS AND COMMUNITIES WITH BETTER INFORMATION ABOUT INSECTS THAT ARE IMPORTANT TO AGRICULTURE AND HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS.

description: ALASKA NATIVE COMMUNITIES FACE SOME OF THE NATION'S HIGHEST RATES OF FOOD INSECURITY, DIET-RELATED CHRONIC DISEASE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL DISRUPTION, YET ALASKA NATIVE PEOPLE REMAIN CRITICALLY UNDERREPRESENTED ACROSS FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND HUMAN SCIENCES (FANH) PROFESSIONS. ALASKA NATIVE STUDENTS FACE SIGNIFICANT STRUCTURAL AND CULTURAL BARRIERS TO DEGREE COMPLETION, AND THE NEED FOR A SKILLED, CULTURALLY GROUNDED FANH WORKFORCE HAS NEVER BEEN MORE URGENT TO ADDRESS ALASKA'S INTERCONNECTED FOOD, HEALTH, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES.GROWING OUR OWN: CULTIVATING ALASKA NATIVE LEADERS IN FANH SCIENCES AND FOOD SOVEREIGNTY WILL ESTABLISH THE ALASKA NATIVE FANH FELLOWS PROGRAM AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA FAIRBANKS (UAF). THIS COHORT-BASED UNDERGRADUATE FELLOWSHIP DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THREE ANNH EDUCATIONAL NEED AREAS: (1) STUDENT RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, AND EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITY; (2) STUDENT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING; AND (3) CURRICULA DESIGN AND MATERIALS DEVELOPMENT.PROJECT OBJECTIVES ARE TO: (1) ESTABLISH AND IMPLEMENT THE ALASKA NATIVE FANH FELLOWS PROGRAM, RECRUITING TWO COHORTS OF EIGHT FELLOWS FROM FANH AND RELATED DEGREE PROGRAMS; (2) BUILD FELLOWS' FANH KNOWLEDGE, LEADERSHIP CAPACITY, AND PROFESSIONAL SKILLS THROUGHA CROSS-DISCIPLINARY SEMINAR, MENTORSHIP, AND A RESEARCH OR EXTENSION APPRENTICESHIP; (3) SUPPORT FELLOWS IN APPLYING THAT KNOWLEDGE THROUGH SELF-DESIGNED, COMMUNITY-ENGAGED LEADERSHIP PROJECTS ADDRESSING LOCALLY IDENTIFIED FOOD, HEALTH, ENVIRONMENTAL, AND FOOD SOVEREIGNTY PRIORITIES; AND (4) EVALUATE AND DISSEMINATE A REPLICABLE, CULTURALLY GROUNDED FANH WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT MODEL.EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE TRAINING 16 ALASKA NATIVE AND RURAL UNDERGRADUATE FELLOWS ACROSS TWO COHORTS, DEVELOPING CULTURALLY GROUNDED FANH EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES, IMPLEMENTING COMMUNITY-ENGAGED LEADERSHIP PROJECTS IN ALASKA NATIVE AND RURAL COMMUNITIES, AND DISSEMINATING A REPLICATION TOOLKIT FOR ANNH-SERVING AND RURAL INSTITUTIONS NATIONWIDE.

description: FISHING IS AN IMPORTANT SOURCE OF HEALTHY AND AFFORDABLE FOOD IN HAWAI'I, AND IS CONNECTED TO LOCAL CULTURE, LIVELIHOODS, THE ECONOMY AND COMMUNITY WELL-BEING. YET, RELATIVELY LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW POLLUTION ENTERING COASTAL WATERS AFFECTS THE QUALITY AND SAFETY OF COMMONLY EATEN REEF FISH. THIS INFORMATION GAP HAS BECOME PARTICULARLY IMPORTANT FOLLOWING EVENTS SUCH AS THE 2023 LAHAINA WILDFIRE, WHEN COMMUNITY MEMBERS RAISED QUESTIONS ABOUT CONTAMINATION OF COASTAL WATERS AND SAFETY OF LOCALLY CAUGHT SEAFOOD. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THESE QUESTIONS WHILE ALSO PREPARING THE NEXT GENERATION OF HAWAI'I PROFESSIONALS TO WORK AT THE INTERSECTION OF COASTAL RESOURCES, FOOD SECURITY AND PUBLIC HEALTH.THE PROJECT WILL BRING TOGETHER EXISTING INFORMATION ON COASTAL WATER QUALITY AND CORAL REEF ECOSYSTEM HEALTH WITH NEW MEASUREMENTS OF CONTAMINANTS IN WATER, SEDIMENT AND COMMONLY CONSUMED REEF FISH IN WEST MAUI. WE WILL ALSO WORK WITH FISHERS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND WHICH FISH PEOPLE EAT, HOW OFTEN THEY EAT THEM, AND HOW LOCALLY CAUGHT SEAFOOD IS SHARED. UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS, AS WELL AS EARLY-CAREER PROFESSIONALS, WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE RESEARCH, ENGAGE WITH COMMUNITY AND AGENCY PARTNERS, AND GAIN HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE THROUGH FIELD, LABORATORY AND OUTREACH ACTIVITIES. PROJECT FINDINGS AND PLACE-BASED LESSONS WILL ALSO BE INCORPORATED INTO UNIVERSITY COURSES, INCLUDING THE NEW FISHERIES GRADUATE PROGRAM. RESULTS WILL BE SHARED WITH COMMUNITIES AND AGENCIES THROUGH MEETINGS, ACCESSIBLE MATERIEALS AND A PUBLIC DECISION-SUPPORT TOOL. ULTIMATELY, THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE COMMUNITIES AND RESOURCE MANAGERS WITH BETTER INFORMATION FOR MAKING DECISIONS ABOUT SEAFOOD CONSUMPTION AND COASTAL RESOURCES, WHILE STRENGTHENING HAWAI?I'S LOCAL WORKFORCE AND CAPACITY TO PROTECT THE NEARSHORE FOOD SYSTEMS ON WHICH COMMUNITIES DEPEND.

description: THE AMERICAN CHESTNUT (CASTANEA DENTATA) WAS ONCE A DOMINANT AND ECOLOGICALLY IMPORTANT TREE SPECIES THROUGHOUT THE EASTERN UNITED STATES BEFORE THE INTRODUCTION OF THE CHESTNUT BLIGHT FUNGUS (CRYPHONECTRIA PARASITICA) FROM ASIA RESULTED IN THE WIDESPREAD MORTALITY OF BILLIONS OF TREES. FOR MORE THAN FOUR DECADES, BREEDING EFFORTS HAVE FOCUSED ON COMBINING THE DISEASE RESISTANCE OF CHINESE CHESTNUT (CASTANEA MOLLISSIMA) WITH THE DESIRABLE GROWTH CHARACTERISTICS, FOREST COMPETITIVENESS, AND GENETIC BACKGROUND OF AMERICAN CHESTNUT. HOWEVER, THE LONG GENERATION TIME OF FOREST TREES AND THE NEED TO EVALUATE LARGE BREEDING POPULATIONS HAVE LIMITED THE SPEED AT WHICH GENETIC IMPROVEMENT CAN BE ACHIEVED. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ACCELERATE GENETIC GAINS IN AMERICAN CHESTNUT HYBRID POPULATIONS BY INTEGRATING RECURRENT GENOMIC SELECTION WITH HIGH-THROUGHPUT REMOTE SENSING-BASED PHENOTYPING.THE PROJECT WILL COMBINE CONTROLLED POLLINATIONS AMONG HIGH-PERFORMING CHESTNUT HYBRIDS, GENOMIC PREDICTION, CONVENTIONAL FIELD EVALUATIONS, AND ADVANCED REMOTE SENSING TECHNOLOGIES TO IMPROVE SELECTION ACCURACY FOR BLIGHT RESISTANCE, TREE GROWTH, AND COMPETITIVE ABILITY. SEEDLING PROGENY FROM SELECTED CROSSES WILL BE GENOTYPED AND EVALUATED USING GENOMIC PREDICTION MODELS TO IDENTIFY INDIVIDUALS WITH SUPERIOR PREDICTED PERFORMANCE WHILE MAINTAINING HIGH LEVELS OF AMERICAN CHESTNUT ANCESTRY. THE HIGHEST-PERFORMING INDIVIDUALS WILL BE ESTABLISHED IN REGIONAL SEED ORCHARDS FOR FUTURE SEED PRODUCTION, WHILE REMAINING PROGENY WILL BE EVALUATED IN REPLICATED PROGENY TRIALS TO IMPROVE GENOMIC PREDICTION MODELS AND QUANTIFY GENETIC GAINS ACROSS BREEDING CYCLES.TO SUPPORT LARGE-SCALE SELECTION AMONG TENS OF THOUSANDS OF CHESTNUT HYBRIDS, THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP AND VALIDATE HIGH-THROUGHPUT PHENOTYPING APPROACHES USING UAS-BASED MULTISPECTRAL, THERMAL, AND THREE-DIMENSIONAL REMOTE SENSING TECHNOLOGIES. THESE APPROACHES WILL ENABLE RAPID, NONDESTRUCTIVE EVALUATION OF TREE HEIGHT, CROWN ARCHITECTURE, BIOMASS DISTRIBUTION, PHYSIOLOGICAL STATUS, AND TRAITS ASSOCIATED WITH BLIGHT RESISTANCE AND FOREST COMPETITIVENESS. REMOTE SENSING-DERIVED PHENOTYPES WILL BE INTEGRATED WITH GENOMIC INFORMATION AND MACHINE LEARNING MODELS TO IMPROVE BREEDING VALUE ESTIMATION AND INCREASE THE EFFICIENCY OF PARENT SELECTION. THE RESULTING GENOMICS-PHENOMICS FRAMEWORK WILL PROVIDE A SCALABLE APPROACH FOR ACCELERATING AMERICAN CHESTNUT IMPROVEMENT AND RESTORATION.THE OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF IMPROVED CHESTNUT GERMPLASM WITH ENHANCED DISEASE RESISTANCE, COMPETITIVE GROWTH CHARACTERISTICS, AND ADAPTATION TO A RANGE OF GROWING CONDITIONS. IMPROVED SEED PRODUCED FROM SELECTED TREES WILL SUPPORT FOREST RESTORATION PLANTINGS AND DISTRIBUTION THROUGH THE AMERICAN CHESTNUT FOUNDATION, ITS REGIONAL CHAPTERS, RESTORATION PARTNERS, GROWERS, AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS THROUGHOUT THE HISTORIC RANGE OF THE AMERICAN CHESTNUT. IN ADDITION, THE DEVELOPED HIGH-THROUGHPUT PHENOTYPING AND GENOMIC S,ELECTION APPROACHES WILL PROVIDE A TRANSFERABLE FRAMEWORK FOR IMPROVING OTHER PERENNIAL TREE SPECIES FACING BIOTIC AND ABIOTIC STRESSES.

description: ALFALFA IS A CORNERSTONE OF THE AGRICULTURAL ECONOMY OF THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST, WITH IDAHO RANKING FIRST IN U.S. PRODUCTION ANNUALLY. AS A PERENNIAL CROP TYPICALLY GROWN FOR FOUR OR MORE YEARS, ALFALFA SERVES AS A SENTINEL HOST THAT ACCUMULATES INSECT-TRANSMITTED PATHOGENS OVER MULTIPLE GROWING SEASONS. DESPITE THE IMPORTANCE OF ALFALFA, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT YIELD AND QUALITY EFFECTS OF PERVASIVE, APHID-VECTORED VIRUSES SUCH AS ALFALFA MOSAIC VIRUS (AMV), BEAN LEAFROLL VIRUS (BLRV), AND PEA STREAK VIRUS (PESV). OUR GROUP RECENTLY FOUND THAT CONVENTIONAL INSECTICIDES CAN REDUCE VECTOR DENSITIES, BUT OFTEN FAIL TO REDUCE VIRUS PREVALENCE OR IMPROVE FORAGE YIELD AND QUALITY IN ESTABLISHED STANDS. THIS PROJECT PROPOSES A NOVEL INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT STRATEGY COMBINING SELECTIVE SOFT INSECTICIDES WITH MINERAL CROP OILS TO SUPPRESS VIRUS TRANSMISSION. THIS APPROACH, SUCCESSFULLY USED IN OUR SEED POTATO STUDIES, USES MINERAL CROP OILS TO INTERFERE WITH APHID PROBING AND VIRION BINDING. OUR PRIMARY OBJECTIVE IS TO EVALUATE THE EFFICACY OF INTEGRATED MINERAL OIL AND SELECTIVE INSECTICIDE ROTATIONS IN REDUCING VIRUS PREVALENCE, SUPPRESSING APHID VECTOR DENSITIES, AND PRESERVING BENEFICIAL ARTHROPODS OVER A FULL THREE-YEAR PRODUCTION CYCLE. WE WILL ALSO CHARACTERIZE THE PREVALENCE OF AMV, BLRV, AND PESV IN COMMERCIAL ALFALFA FIELDS IN IDAHO AND OREGON AND RELATE VIRUS INFECTION TO PRODUCTION AND MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. THIS RESEARCH WILL ENHANCE THE ECONOMIC PROFITABILITY OF GROWERS WHILE ADVANCING SUSTAINABLE INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES FOR ALFALFA PRODUCTION IN THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST.

description: MAINE AND THE WIDER NORTHEAST HAVE A FAST-GROWING SHELLFISH FARMING INDUSTRY, BUT NEARLY ALL OYSTERS AND MUCH OF THE HARVEST ARE SOLD FRESH AND LIVE, ON THE HALF SHELL, THROUGH A SINGLE MARKET. THAT LEAVES GROWERS DANGEROUSLY EXPOSED: WHEN A HARMFUL ALGAE BLOOM FORCES A SHELLFISH-HARVESTING CLOSURE, WHEN A STORM DISRUPTS THE COAST, OR WHEN DEMAND SUDDENLY COLLAPSES--AS IT DID WHEN RESTAURANTS SHUT DOWN DURING THE PANDEMIC--FARMERS CAN LOSE MUCH OF THEIR INCOME ALMOST OVERNIGHT. A MEANINGFUL SHARE OF HARVESTED SHELLFISH IS ALSO DISCARDED SIMPLY BECAUSE IT IS NOT PRETTY ENOUGH FOR THE RAW BAR, EVEN THOUGH IT IS PERFECTLY GOOD, HEALTHY FOOD. CANNING SHELLFISH INTO SHELF-STABLE, PREMIUM TINNED SEAFOOD IS A PROVEN WAY TO ADDRESS THESE PROBLEMS: IT TURNS FORCED DOWNTIME AND DISCARDED PRODUCT INTO SELLABLE INVENTORY, REACHES CUSTOMERS FAR FROM THE COAST, AND STEADIES FARM INCOME. THIS APPROACH HAS STRENGTHENED SEAFOOD COMMUNITIES IN SPAIN AND THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST. YET NORTHEAST PRODUCERS HAVE NEVER HAD THE TESTED RECIPES AND FOOD-SAFETY-APPROVED PROCESSES, THE MARKET EVIDENCE, OR THE BUSINESS NUMBERS THEY NEED TO TRY IT WITH CONFIDENCE. THE STAKES REACH WELL BEYOND INDIVIDUAL FARMS: THIS WORK SUPPORTS COASTAL WORKING WATERFRONTS AND JOBS, REDUCES FOOD WASTE, STRENGTHENS A DOMESTIC SEAFOOD SUPPLY THAT TODAY LEANS HEAVILY ON IMPORTS, AND BUILDS RESILIENCE AGAINST A CHANGING CLIMATE.TO BUILD THAT MISSING FOUNDATION, THE PROJECT BRINGS TOGETHER FOOD SCIENTISTS, A CONSUMER ECONOMIST, AND EXTENSION SPECIALISTS. THE TEAM WILL FIRST ASK MAINE GROWERS DIRECTLY WHAT THEY NEED AND WHAT IS HOLDING THEM BACK. IT WILL THEN DEVELOP AND SAFETY-TEST CANNED SHELLFISH PRODUCTS TOGETHER WITH A COMMERCIAL CANNERY, SO THE RECIPES MEET FEDERAL FOOD-SAFETY REQUIREMENTS. TO LEARN WHETHER CUSTOMERS WILL ACTUALLY BUY THESE PRODUCTS AND WHAT THEY WILL PAY, THE TEAM WILL SURVEY ABOUT 1,500 CONSUMERS AND--UNUSUALLY--HAVE PEOPLE TASTE THE REAL CANNED PRODUCT RATHER THAN SIMPLY REACT TO A LABEL. THOSE FINDINGS FEED A PLAIN-LANGUAGE, FARM-BY-FARM CALCULATOR THAT LETS AN INDIVIDUAL GROWER ENTER THEIR OWN COSTS AND SEE WHETHER CANNING WOULD PAY OFF FOR THEIR OPERATION. GROWERS WILL ALSO VISIT SUCCESSFUL CANNERIES TO SEE THE BUSINESS FIRSTHAND, AND THE LESSONS LEARNED WILL BE PACKAGED INTO AN OPEN, EASY-TO-USE GUIDE AND SHORT TRAINING COURSES.THE ULTIMATE GOAL IS TO GIVE NORTHEAST SHELLFISH FARMERS A PRACTICAL, PROVEN PATH TO DIVERSIFY BEYOND THE FRAGILE FRESH MARKET INTO PREMIUM CANNED PRODUCTS. IF THE PROJECT SUCCEEDS, FARMS WILL HAVE STEADIER INCOME THAT BETTER WITHSTANDS CLOSURES AND MARKET SHOCKS, SHELLFISH THAT WOULD OTHERWISE BE WASTED WILL BECOME NEW REVENUE, AND MAINE CAN BECOME A RECOGNIZED AMERICAN SOURCE OF HIGH-QUALITY CANNED SHELLFISH. THE BROADER BENEFITS INCLUDE NEW AND SUSTAINED COASTAL JOBS, REDUCED DEPENDENCE ON IMPORTED SEAFOOD, LESS FOOD WASTE, AND A MORE RESILIENT REGIONAL FOOD SYSTEM. THE TOOLS, DATA, AND KNOWLEDGE THE PROJECT CREATES ARE DESIGNED TO BE USED ACROSS,THE NORTHEAST AND, ULTIMATELY, BY SHELLFISH-PRODUCING COMMUNITIES NATIONWIDE.

subAgency: National Institute of Food and Agriculture
description: THE ATTRITION RATE OF FOOD ANIMAL VETERINARIANS IS ALARMINGLY HIGH, WITH EARLY CAREER VETERINARIANS FREQUENTLY CITING A LACK OF MENTORSHIP AS A PRIMARY REASON. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT VETERINARY PRACTICES UTILIZING A STRUCTURED MENTORSHIP RESOURCE WILL HAVE INCREASED RETENTION OF NEW ASSOCIATES AND CONSEQUENTLY WE EXPECT A DECREASE IN THE ATTRITION OF FOOD ANIMAL VETERINARIANS FROM THE PROFESSION.BY USING TARGETED SURVEYS TO DEFINE PERSPECTIVE DIFFERENCES BETWEEN MENTORS AND MENTEES, THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A PRACTICAL, STRUCTURED MENTORSHIP TOOLKIT DESIGNED TO FOSTER EFFECTIVE AND SUSTAINABLE RELATIONSHIPS IN FOOD ANIMAL PRACTICE.THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO CREATE AN ELECTRONIC RESOURCE WHICH WILL GUIDE MENTORS AND MENTEES IN DESIGNING INDIVIDUALIZED MENTORSHIP PLANS. IT WILL BE PILOTED IN SELECTED PRACTICES, REFINED BASED ON USER FEEDBACK, AND DISSEMINATED THROUGH PROFESSIONAL ORGANIZATIONS, INDUSTRY NETWORKS, OPEN-ACCESS PUBLICATION, AND CONTINUING EDUCATION EVENTS. ULTIMATELY, THE PROJECT IS INTENDED TO IMPROVE THE ALIGNMENT OF EXPECTATIONS AND ENHANCE JOB SATISFACTION, INCREASING THE RETENTION OF VETERINARIANS WITHIN THE FOOD ANIMAL SECTOR.

description: THE UNITED STATES FACES A CRITICAL SHORTAGE OF VETERINARIANS SERVING LIVESTOCK OPERATIONS, PARTICULARLY IN RURAL COMMUNITIES, LIMITING CATTLE PRODUCERS' ACCESS TO TRAINED PROFESSIONALS WHO CAN PROVIDE REPRODUCTIVE AND HERD HEALTH SERVICES. THIS SHORTAGE IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT BECAUSE THE CATTLE INDUSTRY IS THE LARGEST LIVESTOCK SECTOR IN THE UNITED STATES AND IS WIDELY DISTRIBUTED ACROSS RURAL AREAS, CREATING A SUBSTANTIAL NEED FOR SKILLED VETERINARY SERVICES. LIMITED EXPOSURE TO FOOD-ANIMAL PRACTICE AND INSUFFICIENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR HANDS-ON TRAINING DURING VETERINARY EDUCATION CAN DISCOURAGE STUDENTS FROM PURSUING CAREERS IN LARGE-ANIMAL PRACTICE AND LEAVE NEW GRADUATES WITH LIMITED CONFIDENCE IN PERFORMING REPRODUCTIVE PROCEDURES. TO ADDRESS THIS NEED, FARMVET (FOOD ANIMAL REPRODUCTIVE MANAGEMENT VIA VETERINARY EXPERIENTIAL TRAINING) WILL RECRUIT AND ENGAGE VETERINARY STUDENTS THROUGH EARLY EXPOSURE TO CATTLE PRACTICE, CONNECTIONS WITH PRODUCERS AND INDUSTRY PROFESSIONALS, AND COMPREHENSIVE HANDS-ON TRAINING IN BOVINE REPRODUCTIVE MANAGEMENT AND REPRODUCTIVE TECHNOLOGIES. TRAINING WILL COMBINE CLASSROOM INSTRUCTION, PEER-REVIEWED EDUCATIONAL VIDEOS, DEMONSTRATIONS, AND INTENSIVE, SUPERVISED EXPERIENCE WITH CATTLE TO HELP STUDENTS DEVELOP THE PRACTICAL SKILLS AND CONFIDENCE NEEDED TO PROVIDE REPRODUCTIVE SERVICES AFTER GRADUATION. FARMVET WILL ALSO PROVIDE ADVANCED REPRODUCTIVE TRAINING TO PRACTICING VETERINARIANS AND ARTIFICIAL INSEMINATION TRAINING TO CATTLE PRODUCERS. THE PROGRAM IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE PARTICIPANTS' KNOWLEDGE, PRACTICAL SKILLS, AND CONFIDENCE; EXPAND THE NUMBER OF VETERINARIANS PREPARED TO PROVIDE REPRODUCTIVE SERVICES; AND INCREASE THE NUMBER OF CATTLE PRODUCERS CAPABLE OF SUCCESSFULLY USING ARTIFICIAL INSEMINATION AND RELATED REPRODUCTIVE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. BY STRENGTHENING THE FOOD-ANIMAL VETERINARY WORKFORCE AND INCREASING PRODUCER ACCESS TO REPRODUCTIVE EXPERTISE AND TECHNOLOGIES, FARMVET WILL HELP ADDRESS CRITICAL VETERINARY SERVICE NEEDS WHILE SUPPORTING GENETIC IMPROVEMENT, REPRODUCTIVE EFFICIENCY, AND THE LONG-TERM PRODUCTIVITY AND SUSTAINABILITY OF U.S. CATTLE OPERATIONS.

subAgency: National Institute of Food and Agriculture
description: WE SPEND OVER $50B ON SNACK FOOD EACH YEAR IN AMERICA, AND CALORIES FROM THOSE SNACKS ACCOUNT FOR NEARLY A QUARTER OF OUR DAILY ENERGY, ARE LOW IN NUTRITIONAL VALUE, AND CONTRIBUTE TO OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE. CONSUMER BEHAVIOR IS SHIFTING, BUT MORE NUTRITIOUS HERITAGE GRAINS REMAIN UNDERREPRESENTED, DUE IN PART TO SNACK MANUFACTURING THAT HAS BEEN OPTIMIZED FOR HIGH-STARCH COMMODITY CROPS. THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO BUILD ON THE SUCCESS OF OUR PHASE 1 AWARD USING ADVANCED, PRECISION EXTRUSION TO DE-RISK MANUFACTURING OF NUTRITIONALLY-DENSE SNACKS MADE FROM HERITAGE GRAINS AND PULSES. OBJECTIVES INCLUDE OPTIMIZING EXTRUSION PARAMETERS WITH PRECISION MOISTURE CONTROL, INCREASING PROTEIN CONTENT USING CO-EXTRUSION, MAXIMIZING SHELF LIFE, AND DEVELOPING A SET OF COMMERCIALLY-VALIDATED PROTOCOLS TO ENSURE FOOD SAFETY. IF SUCCESSFUL, COMMERCIALIZATION OF THE INNOVATIONS DESCRIBED IN THIS PROPOSAL WILL INCREASE NUTRITIONAL DENSITY IN SNACK FOODS, STRENGTHEN DEMAND FOR HERITAGE GRAINS, AND BUILD A FOUNDATION FOR LASTING COMMERCIAL SUCCESS ACROSS THE SUPPLY CHAIN. PHASE 1 ACTIVITIES LED DIRECTLY TO THE COMMERCIALIZATION OF A HIGH-PROTEIN, HIGH-FIBER PRODUCT SOLD THROUGHOUT THE NORTHEAST. PHASE II ACTIVITIES WILL BROADEN THE SUITE OF GRAINS OPTIMIZED FOR EXTRUSION, STRENGTHEN PRODUCT-MARKET FIT, AND DEEPEN OUR STRATEGIC POSITIONING USING PRECISION MANUFACTURING TO BRING NEW, HEALTHIER FOODS TO MARKET.

description: MILK IS A VALUABLE SOURCE OF HIGH QUALITY PROTEIN, VITAMINS AND MINERALS AND AN IMPORTANT CONTRIBUTOR TO GLOBAL HEALTH. INFECTIOUS DISEASES IN DAIRY CATTLE CAN SUBSTANTIALLY REDUCE MILK PRODUCTION AND QUALITY, AND HAVE LARGE ECONOMIC IMPACTS. MASTITIS, OR INFECTION OF THE UDDER, IS THE COSTLIEST DISEASE IN DAIRY CATTLE WORLDWIDE; RESULTING IN ANNUAL LOSSES OF UP TO $20 BILLION. THE BACTERIUM STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS IS A TOP CAUSE OF MASTITIS. WE HAVE CONSTRUCTED A VACCINE THAT CAN BE ADMINISTERED TO THE UDDER WITH THE GOAL OF BLOCKING INFECTION. THIS VACCINE IS MADE OF PROTEIN AND CONTAINS A UNIQUE STRUCTURE THAT SUPPORTS THE INDUCTION OF IMMUNITY IN THE BLOOD AS WELL AS LOCAL IMMUNITY IN THE MILK TO PREVENT BOTH BACTERIAL COLONIZATION AND CLINICAL MASTITIS. DELIVERY TO THE UDDER ALSO HAS THE POTENTIAL TO BE A COST-EFFECTIVE ROUTE THAT LEVERAGES CURRENT FARM DRY-OFF PROTOCOLS.OUR GOAL IS TO PRODUCE THIS VACCINE IN A COST-EFFECTIVE WAY AND ESTABLISH ITS SAFETY AND IMMUNOGENICITY TO SUPPORT THE PATH TO LICENSURE. OUR OBJECTIVES ARE TO 1) OPTIMIZE AND SCALE-UP VACCINE PRODUCTION IN THE LABORATORY, AND 2) ESTABLISH THE ROUTE OF VACCINE DELIVERY FOR OPTIMAL IMMUNE INDUCTION. FOR THIS PROJECT WE ARE BUILDING UPON PHASE I OUTCOMES TO VERIFY VACCINE DESIGN USING A LARGE FIELD TRIAL. STUDIES WILL ESTABLISH A PATH TO INDEPENDENCE FOR A START-UP BIOTECH COMPANY, PENTAMER BIOLOGICS, LLC TO FACILITATE CHALLENGE TRIALS FOR VACCINE LICENSURE. THIS RESEARCH SUPPORTS THE MISSION OF USDA NIFA TO ADVANCE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH. AN EFFECTIVE LICENSED VACCINE WILL REDUCE ECONOMIC BURDENS ON FARMERS WHILE INCREASING ANIMAL WELFARE AND IMPROVING FOOD PRODUCTION AND QUALITY.

description: LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS IN CENTRAL FLORIDA WILL CONTINUE TO FACE DIFFICULTY OBTAINING TIMELY VETERINARY CARE BECAUSE FEWER VETERINARIANS ARE AVAILABLE TO SERVE LIVESTOCK, PRODUCERS OFTEN MUST TRAVEL LONG DISTANCES FOR CARE, TRAFFIC CONGESTION INCREASES TRAVEL TIME, AND MANY FARMS LACK ADEQUATE FACILITIES FOR SAFELY HANDLING ANIMALS. THESE CHALLENGES CAN DELAY TREATMENT AND PREVENTIVE CARE, REDUCE ANIMAL HEALTH AND PRODUCTIVITY, AND MAKE IT HARDER FOR PRODUCERS TO MAINTAIN HEALTHY LIVESTOCK. CENTRAL FLORIDA LARGE ANIMAL VETERINARY SERVICES WILL ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES BY EQUIPPING A NEWLY CONSTRUCTED VETERINARY TREATMENT FACILITY WHERE LIVESTOCK CAN BE BROUGHT FOR CARE WHILE ALSO MAINTAINING RELIABLE VETERINARY SERVICES AT FARMS FOR PRODUCERS WHO CANNOT TRANSPORT THEIR ANIMALS. THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE THE PRACTICE'S ABILITY TO PROVIDE TIMELY EXAMINATIONS, PREVENTIVE CARE, DIAGNOSTIC TESTING, TREATMENT, AND SURGERY; INCREASE VETERINARY SERVICE CAPACITY BY 20-30 PERCENT WITHIN THREE YEARS; SERVE 75-100 NEW CLIENTS EACH YEAR; AND PROVIDE 3-5 EDUCATIONAL OR TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES ANNUALLY FOR VETERINARY STUDENTS, INTERNS, AND YOUTH AGRICULTURAL ORGANIZATIONS. BY IMPROVING ACCESS TO VETERINARY CARE AND MAKING SERVICES MORE EFFICIENT, THE PROJECT WILL HELP IMPROVE LIVESTOCK HEALTH AND WELFARE, SUPPORT THE NEEDS OF LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS, STRENGTHEN VETERINARY SERVICES IN RURALREGIONS, AND CONTRIBUTE TO A MORE RESILIENT AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD SYSTEM IN CENTRAL FLORIDA.

description: THE NEED FOR ADDITIONAL FOOD ANIMAL VETERINARIANS IN RURAL SOUTHEAST MINNESOTA IS A REAL AND TANGIBLE PROBLEM ASOLDER VETERINARIANS RETIRE AND CATTLE OPERATIONS CONTINUE TO EXPAND IN SIZE AND NUMBER, LEAVING MANY PRODUCERS WITHOUT EASY ACCESS TO VETERINARY CARE. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IMPROVE AND EXPAND THE AVAILABILITY OF OUR VETERINARY SERVICES TO THE SHORTAGE AREA IN SE MN. IN ORDER TO ACCOMPLISH THIS GOAL, WE PLAN TO HIRE A FORTH QUALIFIED LARGE ANIMAL VETERINARIAN,PROVIDING HIM OR HER WITHA VET-TRUCK AND VET-BOX INSERT. IN ADDITION, WE WILL REPLACE OUR OTHER 3 VET-BOX INSERTS WHICH ARE 30+ YEARS OLDAND FREQUENTLY LAY UP OUR TRUCKS AND VETERINARIANS WITH MAINTENANCE REPAIRS. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL PURCHASE A PORTABLE HYDRAULIC CHUTE WITH TUB & ALLEY TO SERVE OUR CURRENT AND FUTURE CLIENTS WHO DON'T HAVE A WORKING FACILITIES FOR SAFE HANDLING AND PROCESSING OF CATTLE. WITH THESE OBJECTIVES WE EXPECT TO BE MORE EFFICIENT AT MEETING THE NEEDS OF OUR CURRENT AND FUTURE CLIENTS. BY PROVIDING VETERINARY SERVICE TO MORE CLIENTELE IN SE MN WE EXPECT TO HAVE A DIRECT IMPACT ON LOCAL LIVESTOCK HEALTH AND THEREFORE:FOOD SAFETY, PUBLIC HEALTH, AND THE PROFITABILITY OF OUR CLIENTS.

description: MANY TEENAGERS DO NOT MEET THE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR A HEALTHY DIET. INCORPORATING HEALTHY SNACK OPTIONS, SUCH AS WALNUTS, MAY BE ONE WAY TO IMPROVE TEEN'S DIETS AND ENSURE THEY GET IMPORTANT NUTRIENTS. ADDITIONALLY, MOST TEENAGERS DO NOT GET ENOUGH SLEEP, AND CHANGING SLEEP HABITS CAN BE CHALLENGING DUE TO SCHOOL SCHEDULES, COMPETING DEMANDS FROM SOCIAL ACTIVITIES AND SCREENS, AND NORMAL CHANGES IN BIOLOGICAL RHYTHMS THAT HAPPEN DURING ADOLESCENCE. WALNUTS ARE A NATURAL SOURCE OF MELATONIN, A SLEEP HORMONE, AS WELL AS OTHER NUTRIENTS THAT MAY HELP TEENS SLEEP, SUCH AS MAGNESIUM AND POLYUNSATURATED FATTY ACIDS. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO TEST WHETHER REPLACING USUAL EVENING SNACKS WITH A SNACK OF 1 OZ OF WALNUTS WILL IMPROVE TEENS' DIET QUALITY AND SLEEP QUALITY. TO DETERMINE THIS, TEENS WILL COMPLETE TWO, 4-WEEK LONG STUDY SESSIONS WHERE THEY WILL BE RANDOMLY ASSIGNED TO EITHER A) EAT WHATEVER EVENING SNACKS THEY WOULD NORMALLY EAT OR B) REPLACE THEIR EVENING SNACK WITH 1 OZ OF WALNUTS. DURING THE STUDY SESSIONS, TEENS WILL WEAR A SLEEP TRACKER WATCH, KEEP A LOG OF THEIR EVENING SNACKS, COMPLETE SURVEYS ABOUT THEIR SLEEP AND MOOD, AND COMPLETE RECORDS OF THEIR DIETARY INTAKE. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT DURING THE WALNUT INTERVENTION, TEENS WILL HAVE BETTER DIET QUALITY AND BETTER SLEEP QUALITY, COMPARED TO WHEN THEY ARE CONSUMING THEIR USUAL SNACKS. THE RESULTS OF THIS STUDY WILL HELP RESEARCHERS AND NUTRITIONISTS DEVELOP STRATEGIES TO HELP TEENS AND THEIR FAMILIES INCORPORATE HEALTHY SNACKS INTO DAILY ROUTINES TO OPTIMIZE HEALTH AND WELL-BEING.

description: RICE IS A MAJOR STAPLE FOOD CONSUMED BY BILLIONS OF PEOPLE WORLDWIDE AND IS AN IMPORTANT AGRICULTURAL COMMODITY IN ARKANSAS AND THE UNITED STATES. HOWEVER, MOST COMMONLY CONSUMED RICE VARIETIES HAVE A HIGH GLYCEMIC INDEX (GI), MEANING THEY CAN CAUSE A RAPID INCREASE IN BLOOD GLUCOSE LEVELS AFTER CONSUMPTION. FREQUENT CONSUMPTION OF HIGH-GI FOODS IS ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED RISKS OF CHRONIC HEALTH CONDITIONS, INCLUDING TYPE 2 DIABETES, OBESITY, AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. AS THE PREVALENCE AND ECONOMIC BURDEN OF THESE DISEASES CONTINUE TO INCREASE, THERE IS A GROWING NEED TO DEVELOP HEALTHIER STAPLE FOODS THAT SUPPORT IMPROVED DIETARY MANAGEMENT WHILE MAINTAINING CONSUMER ACCEPTANCE. DEVELOPING LOW-GI RICE PRODUCTS CAN PROVIDE NEW MARKET OPPORTUNITIES FOR RICE PRODUCERS AND PROCESSORS, INCREASE THE VALUE OF ARKANSAS-GROWN RICE, AND CONTRIBUTE TO IMPROVED PUBLIC HEALTH OUTCOMES.THIS PROJECT WILL EVALUATE DIFFERENT ARKANSAS RICE VARIETIES TO IDENTIFY THOSE WITH NATURAL CHARACTERISTICS ASSOCIATED WITH LOWER BLOOD GLUCOSE RESPONSES. THE PROJECTWILL ANALYZE THE NUTRITIONAL COMPONENTS OF RICE, INCLUDING STARCH, PROTEIN, FIBER, AND OTHER BENEFICIAL COMPOUNDS, AND EVALUATE HOW THESE COMPONENTS INFLUENCE STARCH DIGESTION AND GI. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO EXAMINE HOW COMMON RICE PROCESSING PRACTICES, SUCH AS PARBOILING, MILLING, AND COOKING, CAN BE ADJUSTED TO SLOW STARCH DIGESTION. SELECTED RICE VARIETIES AND OPTIMIZED PROCESSING APPROACHES WILL THEN BE COMBINED TO DEVELOP RICE PRODUCTS WITH THE LOWEST POSSIBLE GLYCEMIC RESPONSE WHILE MAINTAINING DESIRABLE QUALITY AND CONSUMER ACCEPTANCE.THE EXPECTED OUTCOME OF THIS RESEARCH IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF SCIENCE-BASED RECOMMENDATIONS FOR PRODUCING HEALTHIER, LOW-GI RICE PRODUCTS USING ARKANSAS RICE CULTIVARS AND COMMERCIALLY FEASIBLE PROCESSING METHODS. THE FINDINGS WILL BENEFIT RICE FARMERS, BREEDERS, MILLERS, FOOD PROCESSORS, AND CONSUMERS BY CREATING OPPORTUNITIES FOR VALUE-ADDED RICE PRODUCTS WITH ENHANCED NUTRITIONAL BENEFITS. ULTIMATELY, THIS PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE COMPETITIVENESS OF THE ARKANSAS RICE INDUSTRY, SUPPORT AGRICULTURAL INNOVATION, AND PROVIDE CONSUMERS WITH HEALTHIER FOOD CHOICES THAT MAY HELP REDUCE THE RISK AND MANAGEMENT CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH DIET-RELATED CHRONIC DISEASES.

description: PECAN IS AN IMPORTANT ECONOMIC CROP FOR THE US WITH AN ESTIMATED GLOBAL MARKET VALUE OF ALMOST $1B IN 2025. DESPITE THE HIGH-QUALITY NUTRIENTS AND UNIQUE FLAVOR PROFILE, PECAN NUTS ARE ONLY UTILIZED AS A TOPPING FOR DESSERT AND SNACK (RAW, ROASTED, OR SALTED) AND IN SOME BAKERY AND CONFECTIONERY APPLICATIONS. THERE IS A NEED TO DEVELOP PECAN KERNEL AS HIGH-VALUE FOOD INGREDIENTS. THIS PROJECT WILLDEVELOP HIGH-VALUE PECAN POWDERS WITH EXCELLENT NUTRITIONAL QUALITY AND FUNCTIONALITY. WE WILL ACCOMPLISH THIS BY DETERMINING THE IMPACT OF ISOLATION PH ON PECAN PROTEIN CONCENTRATE, MEASURING DIFFERENT PHYSICOCHEMICAL AND FUNCTIONAL PROPERTIES OF PECAN POWDERS, DETERMINING THE NUTRITIONAL QUALITY OF PECAN POWDERS (AMINO ACID COMPOSITION AND IN VITRO DIGESTIBILITY), AND EVALUATING PRODUCT APPLICATIONS OF PECAN POWDERS IN MUFFINS AND SPONGE CAKES.
